events.title: Blaise Pascal is born
events.description: The French mathematician, physicist and philosopher was born in Clermont-Ferrand. He was a child prodigy who went on to build an early mechanical calculator and to help found probability theory.
events.significance: Pascal's work shaped modern mathematics, the study of fluids and pressure, and French religious philosophy. The unit of pressure is named in his honor.

events.title: Juneteenth: Freedom announced in Galveston, Texas
events.description: Union troops arrived in Galveston, and the news that slavery had ended was announced to the enslaved people of Texas. This came more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation.
events.significance: The date became Juneteenth, the oldest national commemoration of the end of slavery in the United States. It is now a federal holiday.

events.title: Lou Gehrig is born
events.description: Henry Louis Gehrig was born in New York City. He became the Yankees first baseman known as the Iron Horse for his remarkable durability.
events.significance: Gehrig's record streak of consecutive games stood for decades. His career ended with the illness that now bears his name, which brought public attention to ALS.

events.title: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg are executed
events.description: The couple were put to death at Sing Sing Prison in New York. They had been convicted of conspiracy to commit espionage for passing atomic secrets to the Soviet Union.
events.significance: The case came to symbolize Cold War fear and spy paranoia. It remains debated for its fairness and for the severity of the sentences.
